speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and tell me exactly when it started relative to your fever and cold symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The sequence of symptoms—prodrome followed by a facial rash sparing the mouth, then spreading to the trunk and extremities—is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). Do you recall if her cheeks appeared bright red or "slapped" before the body rash appeared, and have you noticed any joint pain or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a prodromal viral illness followed by a "slapped cheek" facial rash and a subsequent pruritic reticular rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
